report.summary: Two separate causes. First, the app leaks books across users (GET /api/books and the /books page return every user's books while the leak_books bug flag is on), which fails the API isolation test and the new-user login test; fix this first in app/main.py list_books, or check whether the CI environment has BUGS=leak_books set, since the workflow file does not set it. Second, both UI add-book tests fail because tests/support/pages.py clicks get_by_test_id('add-books') while the template uses data-testid='add-book'; this is a test bug and a one-line fix.

causes.title: Books of other users are visible to the current user
causes.explanation: list_books() in app/main.py returns every row from the books table when the 'leak_books' seeded bug is active, instead of filtering by owner_id. The API test creates a book as user 1 and then sees its id in user 2's list. The UI login test is the same defect: a brand-new user's /books page renders a row created by another user's test ('From API-d19d31c9'), so the empty-state element is never rendered. With the flag off the code filters by owner (app/main.py:166), so the flag or environment used for this run is the thing to check. The app behaves wrongly whenever the flag is on, so the failing tests are correct to fail.
evidence: tests\api\test_books_api.py:42: AssertionError: assert 2 not in [1, 2] (other user's list contains the book just created by the first user)
app/main.py:11 docstring: 'leak_books  GET /api/books returns every user's books'
app/main.py:163-164: if 'leak_books' in BUGS: rows = conn.execute('SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id').fetchall()
app/main.py:270 render_books uses list_books(user['id']) so the /books page inherits the leak
Login test aria snapshot shows row 'From API-d19d31c9 Robot Delete' on the page of a freshly registered user, and 'Expect to_be_visible get_by_test_id(empty-state)' fails with element(s) not found
Workflow .github/workflows/tests.yml does not set BUGS, so the flag must come from the environment used for this run (BASE_URL or shell env); this is not visible in the failure output
causes.suggested_fix: Fix the app: in list_books always filter by owner_id, and drop or gate the leak_books branch so it is never active outside a deliberate bug-seeding run. Confirm the CI and local environments do not export BUGS=leak_books, or if they do intentionally, mark these tests as expected failures for that configuration. Then rerun the API test and the login test.

causes.title: Page object clicks a data-testid that does not exist in the template
causes.explanation: BooksPage.add() in tests/support/pages.py clicks get_by_test_id('add-books'), but app/templates/books.html defines the submit button as data-testid='add-book'. Playwright waits for the locator for the full 5 s timeout and fails before any app behavior is exercised. The app is correct here; the test helper has a typo. Both UI tests that call add() fail at the same line, so this one fix should clear both.
evidence: Call log: '- waiting for get_by_test_id("add-books")' with Locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded for tests\ui\test_books_ui.py:13 and :42
Grep confirms the only occurrence of 'add-books' is tests/support/pages.py:44, and the only 'add-book' test id is in books.html:9
causes.suggested_fix: In tests/support/pages.py line 44, change get_by_test_id('add-books') to get_by_test_id('add-book'). Rerun tests/ui/test_books_ui.py. The future-year test's later assertions (error text, title kept, no row) are not verified by this run and should be checked after the locator fix.
